fields.questionText: If in the following food chain, 100 J of energy is available to the lion, how much energy was available to the producer? Plants → Deer → Lion
solutionSteps: By the ten per cent law, only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level, so energy at the deer level = 100 J × 10 = 1,000 J.
Energy available to the producer (plants) = 1,000 J × 10 = 10,000 J.

fields.answer: Soil: Pesticides sprayed on crops to protect them from insects settle on the soil particles. Groundwater: Through irrigation and rain water, the pesticides present in the soil seep into the lower layers of soil and reach the groundwater. Water bodies: When waste water or agricultural run-off is drained into water bodies like rivers, canals and ponds, the pesticides reach these water bodies.
solutionSteps: Soil: Pesticides sprayed on crops to protect them from insects settle on the soil particles.
Groundwater: Through irrigation and rain water, pesticides in the soil seep into lower layers and reach the groundwater.
Water bodies: Waste water and agricultural run-off carrying pesticides are drained into rivers, canals and ponds, so the pesticides reach these water bodies.
fields.finalAnswer: Pesticides settle on soil, seep down to groundwater with irrigation/rain water, and reach rivers, canals and ponds with waste water and agricultural run-off.

fields.answer: Autotrophs are organisms that make their own food from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, e.g. green plants. Heterotrophs cannot make their own food by photosynthesis and depend on other organisms for food, e.g. animals. Decomposers break down the complex organic molecules in the dead remains of plants and animals into simpler substances, e.g. bacteria and fungi.
solutionSteps: Autotrophs: organisms that make their own food from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll. Example: green plants.
Heterotrophs: organisms that cannot make their own food by photosynthesis and depend on other organisms for food. Example: animals (e.g. goat, lion).
Decomposers: organisms that break down complex organic molecules in the dead remains of plants and animals into simpler substances. Example: bacteria, fungi.
fields.finalAnswer: Autotrophs make their own food (green plants); heterotrophs depend on others for food (animals); decomposers break down dead remains into simple substances (bacteria, fungi).

fields.questionText: Write one difference between biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes. List two impacts of each type of the accumulated waste on environment if not disposed off properly.
fields.answer: Biodegradable wastes can be broken down by biological processes (by micro-organisms such as bacteria and fungi), whereas non-biodegradable wastes cannot be broken down by biological processes. Impacts of accumulated biodegradable waste: (i) foul smell; (ii) breeding place for disease-carrying organisms such as flies and mosquitoes. Impacts of accumulated non-biodegradable waste: (i) biological magnification of harmful chemicals; (ii) loss of soil fertility.
solutionSteps: Difference (1 mark): Biodegradable wastes can be broken down by biological processes (micro-organisms); non-biodegradable wastes cannot be broken down by biological processes.
Impacts of accumulated biodegradable waste (½ + ½ mark): (i) foul smell; (ii) breeding place for carriers of diseases (flies, mosquitoes). (Or any other valid impact.)
Impacts of accumulated non-biodegradable waste (½ + ½ mark): (i) biological magnification; (ii) loss of soil fertility. (Or any other valid impact.)
fields.finalAnswer: Biodegradable waste is broken down by micro-organisms, non-biodegradable is not. Biodegradable: foul smell, breeding of disease carriers. Non-biodegradable: biological magnification, loss of soil fertility.

fields.questionText: Explain how some harmful chemicals enter our bodies through the food chain. Why is the concentration of these harmful chemicals found to be maximum in human beings?
fields.answer: Harmful chemicals such as pesticides used to protect crops are washed into the soil and water bodies, absorbed by plants along with water and minerals, and taken up by animals; when we eat these plants and animals, the chemicals enter our bodies. Since these chemicals are non-biodegradable, they accumulate at each trophic level (biological magnification); as human beings occupy the top level in the food chain, the maximum concentration accumulates in them.
solutionSteps: Some harmful substances like pesticides are used to protect crops; they are washed down into the soil or water bodies.
They are absorbed by plants along with water and minerals and by animals from water; when we consume these food items, the pesticides enter our body.

Being non-biodegradable, they accumulate progressively at each trophic level (biological magnification); as human beings occupy the top level in the food chain, the maximum concentration accumulates in them.
fields.finalAnswer: Pesticides pass from soil/water into plants and animals and then into us through food; being non-biodegradable they accumulate at each trophic level, so humans at the top have the maximum concentration.
